title: Language reference
body:
This reference describes the implemented subset, not every statement from the named machines. The profile chapters identify vocabulary restrictions and semantic differences.

Source and values

Each logical source record must start with an integer line number 1–65529. Lines are sorted numerically; repeated numbers replace earlier ones, and bare numbers delete. Physical multiline strings/records are unsupported and are never silently repaired. Colon separates statements. REM consumes the remainder of its line. Keywords are case-insensitive; quoted literal text preserves case. No immediate expression execution exists at READY.

Numeric literals accept decimal and E exponent notation. Ordinary numeric values use finite JavaScript doubles; Tiny truncates numeric results. Strings use double quotes and concatenate with +. BASIC strings are limited to 4096 characters. Variables default to 0 or an empty string. MS/TRS names have two significant characters; Tiny has one; Simple Web Basic preserves complete case-sensitive names. See TRS for explicit types.

Statements

SyntaxMeaning
[LET] A=expressionAssign a scalar or array element, checking its value type.
PRINT expression; expression, expressionSemicolon joins output; comma advances a print zone (profile dependent); final separator suppresses newline. Bare PRINT emits a newline. ? is a shorthand.
INPUT ["prompt";] A,B$Pause for typed values. Quoted CSV can include commas. Profile differences apply to case, blank entries and partial input.
IF test THEN statement [ELSE statement]Zero is false. THEN line-number is a jump. Nested branches and colon-separated branches are supported. TRS also accepts omitted THEN.
GOTO line / GOSUB line / RETURNJump; call a subroutine; return to its saved continuation. Target expressions must identify an existing line.
ON expression GOTO/GOSUB a,b,cTruncated one-based selector; outside the list continues without a jump.
FOR I=start TO end [STEP increment] / NEXT [I]Loop with an inclusive end test at NEXT. STEP defaults to 1 and cannot be zero. NEXT advances before testing; loops can execute once even when their initial bound is already exceeded.
DIM A(10),B(2,3)Zero-based inclusive bounds; up to four dimensions and 16384 total cells. Undimensioned arrays implicitly use bound 10 per dimension. Duplicate DIM fails.
DATA values / READ A,B$ / RESTORE [line]DATA is nonexecuting stored text. READ converts to destination type. RESTORE resets, or seeks the first DATA at/after its line. Out of DATA fails.
DEF FNS(X)=expression / FNS(value)Single-argument expression function. Its parameter temporarily shadows the variable and is restored afterward.
STOP / ENDSTOP permits CONT; END ends normally. Falling beyond the last line also ends.
REM textComment to end of line.

TRS adds DEFINT, DEFSNG, DEFDBL, DEFSTR, CLEAR, CLS, PRINT @, PRINT#, INPUT#, OPEN and CLOSE; see its profile and the device reference. Simple Web Basic vocabulary is narrower than the shared AST grammar.

Operators

Arithmetic: + - * / ^ MOD; division/modulo by zero fails. Comparison: = <> < > <= >=, requiring like types. Boolean/bit operations: AND OR NOT, evaluated eagerly without short-circuiting. Parentheses override precedence. Historical profiles order OR, AND, comparisons, addition, multiplication/division/MOD, unary signs, exponentiation; NOT binds to comparisons. Exponentiation associates right. Simple Web Basic puts AND and OR together, exponentiation with multiplication, and unary signs above those. Use parentheses when moving between profiles.

Built-in functions

FunctionArguments and result
ABS(x), SGN(x), INT(x)Absolute value, sign (-1/0/1), floor toward negative infinity.
SQR(x), SIN(x), COS(x), TAN(x), ATN(x)Square root and trigonometry in radians. Invalid/nonfinite results fail.
LOG(x), EXP(x)Natural logarithm and exponential; finite result required.
RND(x)Profile-dependent; see dialect chapters. Uses the configured seeded generator.
LEN(s), ASC(s), CHR$(n)Length; first character code (nonempty string); character code 0–255, truncated. Display sanitizes non-ASCII/control characters, so not all codes render as hardware glyphs.
LEFT$(s,n), RIGHT$(s,n)First/last n characters; nonnegative truncated length.
MID$(s,start[,n])One-based start and optional nonnegative truncated length.
STR$(x), VAL(s)Numeric string (historical positive leading space) and numeric prefix conversion; VAL returns zero if no numeric prefix.
TAB(n), SPC(n)Spacing strings; TAB targets a column and does not move backward. Bounds remain enforced.
CINT(x), FIX(x), CSNG(x), CDBL(x)TRS-only: signed 16-bit floor, truncate toward zero, host numeric identity for single/double conversion.
POS(0), EOF(channel)TRS-only: logical column modulo 64; -1 at end of readable virtual file, otherwise 0.
MEMRecognized only to report that a ROM memory layout is unavailable; no fabricated result.

Expected arity is checked. Simple Web Basic supports only its listed vocabulary; Tiny string variables are unavailable even though quoted PRINT text and some shared expression functions parse. Such extensions do not imply historical Tiny fidelity.

Limits

Per run: 1,000,000 statements and 1,000,000 expression evaluations; 2000 ms active execution time; 131072 output characters; 16384 array cells; 1024 scalars; 128 stack frames; expression depth 64. Source: 131072 characters, 4096 lines, 8192 characters per line, 4096 tokens per line. Input: 4096 characters. UI scrollback is separately bounded. These limits are enforced rather than disabled for long programs.
